The challenge in this first appeal is to the award passed by  the reference Court dated 02.05.2008, by which, the reference Court has  awarded enhanced compensation to the amount of Rs. 5,79,154/- along  with solatium and the interest.
The LAR no. 92/2001, is impugned in the  this First Appeal.
Being dissatisfied, the present application is being  preferred.
2. The land of the present appellant / original claimant was  acquired for Lower Dudhna Project.

So far as land of the appellant is  concerned, it was in a field Survey No. 63/1, village Kedarwakadi,
 admeasuring 5.67 HR.

sentences.text: 5. Per Contra
Mr. Deshpande, has contended that few First Appeals decided by this Court.
Those First Appeals were challenged before the Hon'ble Apex Court by the claimants but the Hon'ble Apex Court had rejected those First Appeals and the Special Leave Petitions were dismissed.
He has produced that order on record.
He stated that order dated 15.12.2017, passed in Special Leave Petition (Civil) Diary No. 34448/2017, by the Hon'ble Apex Court is crystal clear.

He has tendered the copy of the order dated 15.12.2017, passed in SLP (Civil)
Diary No. 34448/2017, which is reproduced as under :
 "UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  ORDER Delay condoned.

The special leave petitions are dismissed."
6.
In the aforesaid background, I have gone through the record of the case.

Admittedly, by way of acquisition of land, the claimants are deprived of their property and, therefore, the pieces of the land were separately categorized and compensation was accordingly, paid based on the category determined by the reference Court.
Order passed by Hon'ble Apex Court dated 25.02.2026, is crystal clear and also governs issue involved in present case.

Hence, I am inclined to pass the following order:
6 53FA458.2019.odt ORDER i.
First Appeal is allowed.

ii. The claimant shall be entitled for the compensation for the nature of land which was decided by the reference Court i.e. if dry land Rs. 2400/-, if semi-irrigated land Rs. 3600/-, if fully irrigated land Rs. 4800/- and if Pot Kharab land Rs. 1200/-. iii.

The appellant shall be entitled to the interest under Sections 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act as per the Full Bench Judgment of this Court in the case of State of Maharashtra Vs. Kailash Shiva Rangari, 2016 AIR (Bom.) 141. iv.

sentences.text: The appellant shall not be entitled to the interest and the statutory benefits for the delayed period.

v.
Save
and except above, the impugned judgment and award passed by the Reference Court shall stand unaltered.
vi. The appellant shall pay deficit court fees.
vii. Award be drawn accordingly.
